top.title: 2027: Any Igbo against Obi is enemy of Ndigbo – Victor Umeh
top.description: Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central Senatorial District, has declared that any Igbo person opposed to the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi, is an enemy of Ndigbo. Umeh, who described Obi as the conscience of the Igbo people, also cautioned political leaders in the South-East, particularly the Anambra State Government, against working against the former governor’s presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The senator, popularly known as Ohamadike, made the remarks in a trending video, on Monday. He said Obi represented the collective aspirations of the Igbo people and urged the people of the South-East to rally behind him. “I’m an Igbo activist, you people know me and you hear my voice in the Senate on all issues of national importance. Peter is our conscience in this election. Any Igbo man who stands up to say we will not vote for Peter Obi, I’m telling you that he’s an enemy of Igbo people,” Umeh said. He specifically warned the Anambra State Government against allegedly opposing Obi’s ambition for political reasons, arguing that the state’s leadership should consider the broader interests of the Igbo people. Umeh claimed he played a significant role in the emergence of Governor Chukwuma Soludo, insisting that the office of governor was held in trust for the collective interest of the people. “This government in the state, I helped installing it. Nobody came here the governor of Anambra State since 2003 without my input. This one that is serving, I was a principal contributor to his ascending to that office. He’s holding that office on trust for all of us,” he said. The senator urged Soludo not to undermine Obi’s presidential ambition, describing any attempt to work against his kinsman as an abomination. “Let him not commit what is called abomination by wanting to destroy his brother in the name of politics,” he warned. Umeh further argued that if politicians from other geopolitical zones were free to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu, Igbo people should equally be allowed to rally behind Obi without intimidation or condemnation. Recalling Obi’s support for him, the senator called on Ndigbo to stand for what he described as truth and justice, adding that Obi’s success in the 2027 presidential election would be a collective achievement for the South-East. “He told me this is his time and if he makes it, the Igbos have made it. So let nobody come and insult us and our intelligence,” Umeh added. The post 2027: Any Igbo against Obi is enemy of Ndigbo – Victor Umeh appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Here are the price-matching policies for Best Buy, Walmart, and others
top.description: Nothing is more frustrating than buying a new pair of headphones or an OLED TV, only to find out you could have gotten it cheaper somewhere else a few days or weeks later. That’s why, to keep customers happy and prevent them from shopping elsewhere, some retailers offer price-matching policies that promise to match a lower price found elsewhere. That kind of information comes in handy year-round, but it’s especially helpful during the weeks of deals leading up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Below are the price-matching policies for several major retailers. A few things to note: First, each retailer has its own set of rules and restrictions. We’ve summarized some of them here, but we recommend visiting the provided links and reading the policies carefully. Second, most retailers that serve as marketplaces for other sellers, including wholesale retailers like Costco, don’t offer protections, and many traditional stores won’t match their prices. Lastly, there are always exceptions to the rules. If you’re looking for a deal on a product and you know it’s available for a lower price elsewhere (or it was previously offered at the same retailer), it never hurts to call or chat with a customer service rep and ask if they’ll match the price. You have nothing to lose but time, and there’s always a chance they may find a loophole or make a special exception. Amazon Amazon doesn’t offer price matching. Full stop. You can contact customer support, but even if you’re an Amazon Prime customer, they likely won’t help. top.title: U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have formally withdrawn a 2020 proposal that would have cut the Bank Secrecy Act threshold for cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250 and spelled out that the rules cover crypto, leaving the existing $3,000 line in place. The notice, published Monday in the Federal Register, says the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Fed’s Board of Governors “will not take further action” on a proposal they first issued on Oct. 27, 2020. That plan would have lowered the recordkeeping and Travel Rule thresholds to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. Those rules require banks and nonbank financial institutions to collect, retain and pass along customer information on transfers of $3,000 or more. It also would have clarified the meaning of “money” in both rules so they apply to transactions involving convertible virtual currency, along with digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. Why the agencies backed off Per the notcie, FinCEN and the Fed received nearly 3,000 comments on the proposal, most of them substantially similar form letters. Commenters generally opposed the lower threshold, arguing that it would burden smaller institutions and could push consumers sending remittances toward less regulated channels. Many also noted that potentially illicit transfers below $3,000 were already being flagged to FinCEN through suspicious activity reports. Several said the threshold should rise instead, citing inflation since 1995. Sentiment on the crypto language was mixed. Companies that provide crypto services and their trade groups opposed it, citing technical limits and the lack of an international messaging standard for crypto transfers, while some banks and money services businesses supported it. The agencies gave two reasons for pulling the proposal. More than five years have passed, and they said more public feedback would help before adopting anything similar. The withdrawal, they wrote, gives the public “certainty” that no final rule will be issued without another chance to comment. The second reason is the crypto industry itself. The notice says crypto markets “have continued to mature” and new legal frameworks are emerging, citing the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted on July 18, 2025. Any future change tied to crypto, the agencies said, should be considered in light of those developments so it is “fit for purpose.” What the withdrawal does and does not do The notice does not repeal or amend any rule. The $3,000 threshold that has applied for decades stays where it is, and so does the existing Travel Rule. What disappears is the specific path to $250 and the proposed wording that would have written crypto into the definition of money. top.title: FG considers assessment tests for Nigerians with foreign degrees before NYSC
top.description: The Federal Government is considering the introduction of assessment test for Nigerians who obtain degrees from foreign institutions, particularly in African countries. Dr Folake Olatunji-David, Acting Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Education, disclosed this at the 37th meeting of the National Standing Committee (NSC) on Evaluation of Foreign Qualifications in Abuja on Monday. Olatunji-David said the assessment test was necessary before their qualifications would be evaluated for mobilisation into the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). She said the proposal was aimed at ensuring that foreign qualifications presented by Nigerians reflected genuine learning achievements and met the required academic standards. She explained that the measure was particularly important given the increasing number of Nigerians studying in foreign higher institutions, especially in West Africa. “We must ensure that the standard of education in Nigeria is not lowered by allowing all manner of foreign qualifications that are not recognised to be paraded by Nigerians without the corresponding learning achievement. “In as much as we want to encourage global socialisation, education, and the rest of them because the world is a global village now, but we want to maintain standard. “We want to ensure that, yes, for every certificate given, they are earned, and they can produce people that can contribute positively to our national development. “I therefore invite this committee once again to consider, if necessary, an assessment test before such graduates are evaluated for NYSC,” she said. Olatunji-David described the committee as central to efforts to safeguard the integrity of Nigeria’s education system by ensuring that only genuine and duly accredited foreign qualifications were recognised. She expressed concern over the rising cases of forgery of Nigerian and foreign degree certificates, saying the ministry was taking steps to address the menace. The acting permanent secretary commended members of the committee for decisions reached at their previous meeting, describing them as important steps towards improving the evaluation and accreditation of foreign qualifications. She said the ministry had recorded progress in confirming the accreditation status of foreign institutions, issuing clearance letters for NYSC mobilisation, authenticating certificates and issuing no-objection letters. top.title: Incident-by-incident: Was it a bad weekend for VAR?
top.description: Manchester United's last-gasp equaliser against Aston Villa survived a VAR review for a potential foul [Getty Images] Whisper it quietly, but the statistics say video assistant referee decisions have been pretty good in the Premier League so far this season. The Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel, which looks at every contentious decision and votes whether it is right or wrong, reported just two VAR errors after eight rounds of matches. At the same stage last season, there had been six mistakes. Then came this weekend, during which almost every top-flight game had a controversial decision. BBC Sport looks at most of these situations - there really were too many to do them all - and assesses the likelihood that the KMI Panel will add to the list of errors. Manchester United 4-4 Aston Villa Incident 1: Penalty awarded to Manchester United for a foul by Boubacar Kamara on Matheus Cunha in the 16th minute. Verdict: The spot-kick was awarded because the Villa defender went through Cunha to win the ball. Replays clearly showed the first contact was on the Brazilian's foot. What the KMI Panel might say: This will be a correct decision. Incident 2: Possible foul by Senne Lammens on Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki before Patrick Dorgu's 96th-minute equaliser. Verdict : There are similarities to a goal Arsenal scored at Old Trafford last season, when William Saliba leant into United goalkeeper Altay Bayındır. Lammens was not looking at the ball, which increases the chances of a VAR intervention. What the KMI Panel might say: With the higher bar for an intervention in the Premier League, and minimal contact, it is unlikely to be a VAR error not to disallow the goal. Arsenal 1-0 Hull Incident: Kai Havertz was pulled down inside the area by Nobel Mendy. The VAR, Michael Oliver, sent referee Farai Hallam to the pitchside monitor for a penalty, but it was not given due to an offside offence by the Germany international. top.title: Kettering Town 'can not hide' from its racism problem
top.description: Kettering Town's director of football said the club could no longer hide behind "the comforting lie" that the abuse came from "a small minority" [Getty Images] Non-league Kettering Town have said they "can no longer hide" from the issue of racism after a visiting player was allegedly subjected to "sickening" abuse. Redditch United player Dan Sweeney said he was targeted by a Kettering supporter during Saturday's Southern League Premier Division Central tie at the Poppies' Latimer Park stadium, which the hosts won 2-1. The incident comes after a match official reported alleged racial abuse at a Kettering fixture last season , and a previous instance of alleged racist abuse against a Redditch player at Latimer Park in 2017 . In a statement, Kettering director of football Fabian Forde said the "poison" of racism went beyond matchdays. He also spoke out against the presence of what he called "festering" racism on the club's fans forums. Writing on the club's website , Forde said: "Let's be completely honest with ourselves: this is not the first time. We can no longer hide behind the comforting lie that 'it's just a small minority' or 'they don't reflect the majority of our fans'. "Every single time we dismiss hate by calling it a minority issue, we minimise the damage. The truth is, if the majority stays silent, that small minority becomes our identity. "They tarnish our reputation in the eyes of opposition players, fans, and officials. They make our club look like a haven for bigotry. Is that really who we want to be?" Forde added that the club could not "keep sending out generic statements that mean nothing" and urged fans to support "real cultural change" by taking responsibility for calling out the perpetrators of racist abuse. He said: "To the majority of our fans, the good, decent people who love this club for the right reasons, we are pleading with you. "We need you to stand up. We need you to confront this minority head-on. If you see someone typing hate online, call them out. If you hear someone shouting abuse next to you on a Saturday afternoon, don't look away. "Tell a steward. Identify them to the club. Why are we protecting people who are actively destroying the reputation of the club we love?" Northamptonshire Police said Saturday's alleged incident had not yet been reported to officers [Getty Images] In relation to Saturday's incident, Northamptonshire Police said they had "not identified any report relating to this allegation." However, the force said: "It may be that any report is awaiting allocation or has been made to another police force. Should a report be made elsewhere and the alleged offence be found to have taken place within Northamptonshire, we would take ownership of the investigation. "We note Kettering Town FC's statement that it is working with its security team, stewards and the relevant authorities to identify those responsible, and we would encourage anyone who believes they have been the victim of a crime to report

top.title: Titans WR had 'incident' involving law enforcement at Nashville airport
top.description: The bye week was not all quiet for the Tennessee Titans . Wide receiver Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident at Nashville International Airport over the weekend, with details remaining scant other than the Titans acknowledging they are aware of the "incident" and are communicating with the Metro Nashville Airport Authority. "With regards to Calvin, we’re aware of everything that’s happening. From my understanding, it was a very minor miscommunication at the airport," Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday, Nov. 9. "Unfortunately, the law enforcement (agencies) have it, and that’s about as far as I can go with commenting." Ridley has six catches for 91 yards in seven games this season and could be a candidate to be moved to another team prior to Tuesday's trade deadline. The Titans are coming off their extended rest with a 1-7 record and heading into a Nov. 15 matchup against the AFC South's first-place Jacksonville Jaguars . It has not been a smooth season for Tennessee. The Titans released defensive lineman Jordan Elliott last month after he pulled a gun and threatened a teammate in the parking lot of the team's facility. Saleh was asked if the latest Ridley development was "frustrating," but the former head coach of the New York Jets would not go that far. “I think when you’re losing everything’s exacerbated, but all thirty-two teams deal with things throughout the season," Saleh said. "But yeah, it’s unfortunate with what happened.” A first-round pick of the Atlanta Falcons in 2018, Ridley has also played for the Jacksonville Jaguars and Tennessee Titans. He served a suspension during the 2022 season for betting on NFL games while he was injured the previous season. This is his third season of a four-year, $92 million contract he signed with Tennessee. nigeria.title: 2027: Any Igbo against Obi is enemy of Ndigbo – Victor Umeh
nigeria.description: Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central Senatorial District, has declared that any Igbo person opposed to the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi, is an enemy of Ndigbo. Umeh, who described Obi as the conscience of the Igbo people, also cautioned political leaders in the South-East, particularly the Anambra State Government, against working against the former governor’s presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The senator, popularly known as Ohamadike, made the remarks in a trending video, on Monday. He said Obi represented the collective aspirations of the Igbo people and urged the people of the South-East to rally behind him. “I’m an Igbo activist, you people know me and you hear my voice in the Senate on all issues of national importance. Peter is our conscience in this election. Any Igbo man who stands up to say we will not vote for Peter Obi, I’m telling you that he’s an enemy of Igbo people,” Umeh said. He specifically warned the Anambra State Government against allegedly opposing Obi’s ambition for political reasons, arguing that the state’s leadership should consider the broader interests of the Igbo people. Umeh claimed he played a significant role in the emergence of Governor Chukwuma Soludo, insisting that the office of governor was held in trust for the collective interest of the people. “This government in the state, I helped installing it. Nobody came here the governor of Anambra State since 2003 without my input. This one that is serving, I was a principal contributor to his ascending to that office. He’s holding that office on trust for all of us,” he said. The senator urged Soludo not to undermine Obi’s presidential ambition, describing any attempt to work against his kinsman as an abomination. “Let him not commit what is called abomination by wanting to destroy his brother in the name of politics,” he warned. Umeh further argued that if politicians from other geopolitical zones were free to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu, Igbo people should equally be allowed to rally behind Obi without intimidation or condemnation. Recalling Obi’s support for him, the senator called on Ndigbo to stand for what he described as truth and justice, adding that Obi’s success in the 2027 presidential election would be a collective achievement for the South-East. “He told me this is his time and if he makes it, the Igbos have made it. nigeria.title: ICPC files amended charge against Adeyemi, adds four civil servants
nigeria.description: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has filed amended charges against Adeniyi Adeyemi, the purported director general of the non-existent Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council (PFIPC). The prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, told the court that ICPC expanded the previous 22 counts to 36. Tahir said that the four suspects are Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe and included in the new charge. The case was originally filed by the Nigerian police. Monday’s proceedings, which originally slated for hearing of Adeyemi’s bail application, was halted because of the charge amendment, requiring all defendants, including Adeyemi, to enter their pleas. However, the plea taking could not proceed because the fourth defendant, Omameh, was absent from court on health grounds. The rest of the defendants were in court. ”Her unavailability in court has constrained the prosecution from proceeding with the arraignment, this being a criminal charge,” Tahir said. He relied on Section 266 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) for his application. Tahir argued that an accused person has to be present in court throughout the trial, “subject to the exception stated therein.” He, therefore, urged the court for a short adjournment to allow the fourth defendant time to recover and enter her plea. Adeyemi’s counsel, Ibrahim Angulu, SAN, did not object to the amended charge or adjournment. However, he reminded the court of Adeyemi’s prolonged detention. Meanwhile, Justice Yusuf Halilu adjourned until Nov. 18 for the arraignment of the suspects. He, however, ordered that Adeyemi should be taken back to Kuje Correctional Facility and the other defendants to return to the ICPC detention facility. nigeria.title: Youth Olympics: Nwankwo, Bright Win Historic Gold In Men’s, Women’s 100m
nigeria.description: Nigeria made an impressive start to the athletics competition at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Sunday, winning gold in both the men’s and women’s 100m finals at the Complexe Iba Mar Diop. Rosemary Nwankwo opened the country’s gold-medal account in the women’s 100m, crossing the finish line in 11.16 seconds to claim victory and set a new personal best. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, gold medalist (C), Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates (L), silver medalist, and Dana Salem of Qatar (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) She finished ahead of Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates, who clocked 11.41 seconds, also a personal best, while Dana Salem of Qatar settled for bronze in 11.48 seconds. The win made Nwankwo the third Nigerian woman to take Youth Olympic 100m gold, following Josephine Omaka at the inaugural Singapore 2010 Games and Rosemary Chukwuma at Buenos Aires 2018. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, winner of the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, poses next to the board at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) Nigeria’s celebrations continued minutes later as Gift Bright secured another gold medal in the men’s 100m, finishing in a personal-best time of 10.28 seconds. China’s Zhang Hangyu came second in 10.57 seconds, while Poland’s Szymon Dolega claimed bronze in 10.61 seconds. Speaking after her triumph, Nwankwo said she remained focused on her race despite the significance of the occasion. Nigeria’s Gift Bright, react after winning the men’s 100-meter semifinal at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) “There was no pressure on me. I run my race. I focused on me, and I did it,” she said. “I’ve prayed for this moment, and I did it.” For Bright, the victory was particularly significant after a thigh injury had troubled him in the two weeks leading up to the competition. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) He admitted that the injury had affected his confidence but said he was relieved to compete without pain in the final. “I want to tell you guys that at the next (Youth) Olympics, expect Nigeria to win it again. We are good sprinters,” he said. We know how to condition ourselves to stay where we are. nigeria.title: PIA: Reps demand accountability, measurable benefits for Nigerians
nigeria.description: …Say five years after enactment, reforms must boost production, revenue, investment By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for greater accountability in the management of Nigeria’s petroleum resources, insisting that the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) must deliver increased oil production, higher government revenue, improved energy security, job creation and tangible benefits for Nigerians. The Speaker noted that the transformation of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation into NNPC Ltd, the establishment of regulatory institutions and the introduction of a framework for host community development were intended to address longstanding challenges in the petroleum sector. He, however, stressed that the passage of the legislation must be followed by effective implementation to achieve its objectives. “The passage of a reform law is not the same as the successful implementation of that reform,” Abbas said. Obi described the incident as another example of what he called the growing culture of “toxic politics” in Nigeria, alleging that he had experienced similar treatment during a previous visit to a football event. nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Ogun State Government has described a viral video showing prospective corps members sleeping in a hall at the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) Orientation Camp in Sagamu, following concerns over accommodation conditions at the facility. The state government said the situation occurred during the registration exercise, which extended into the night, adding that the allocation of hostels and screening of prospective corps members were the exclusive responsibilities of NYSC officials. Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to Governor Dapo Abiodun, Kayode Akinmade, in a Facebook post on Monday, explained that prospective corps members were required to undergo credential verification and screening before being assigned accommodation. He said those whose registration extended into the night were temporarily accommodated in the multipurpose hall, where mattresses were provided for them to rest while the exercise continued. He stated: “The video captured a temporary arrangement during the registration exercise, which continued into the night. “The prospective corps members must first undergo credential verification and screening by NYSC officials before being allocated hostels. Those whose registration extended into the night were temporarily accommodated in the multipurpose hall, with mattresses provided for them to rest while the exercise continued.” Akinmade noted that Ogun State received more than 4,300 prospective corps members in the current batch, compared with slightly over 2,000 in previous batches, putting additional pressure on available camp facilities. He stressed that although NYSC handles registration, screening and hostel allocation, the state government supports the scheme through interventions aimed at improving the welfare of corps members. According to him, the state government provided 500 mattresses for the current exercise, while the Akarigbo of Remo donated 100 mattresses, followed by an additional 200. Akinmade also recalled that Governor Abiodun recently approved a ₦50,000 welfare grant for each of the 3,050 corps members in the 2026 Batch C, Stream I, to support their transportation. He added that Ogun State had been adjudged the best in the country in NYSC administration, describing the recognition as a reflection of the government’s sustained commitment to the scheme. The government urged the public to distinguish between the operational responsibilities of NYSC and the supportive role of the state, assuring that the Abiodun administration would continue to provide an enabling environment for corps members serving in Ogun. nigeria.description: Nigeria and France have emerged as the only two countries to have won both the men’s and women’s FIFA Under-17 World Cups following the Flamingos’ historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Nigeria achieved the milestone after its U-17 women’s team defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Rabat, becoming the first African nation to win the women’s competition. The victory also ended Nigeria’s 18-year wait for a FIFA U-17 title, having last won the men’s competition in 2015. According to FIFA’s records, France were previously the only country to have won both versions of the tournament, having secured the men’s title in 2001 and the women’s trophy in 2012. Nigeria’s five men’s U-17 World Cup titles Nigeria’s success in the men’s competition dates back to 1985, when the Golden Eaglets defeated West Germany 2-0 in Beijing to win the inaugural edition of the tournament, then known as the FIFA U-16 World Championship. The team went on to win the competition four more times, in 1993, 2007, 2013 and 2015. Its five titles make Nigeria the most successful country in the history of the men’s U-17 World Cup. The 2013 triumph came after a 3-0 victory over Mexico in the final, while the 2015 team defeated Mali 2-0 in Chile to become the first country to win consecutive editions of the tournament. How France achieved the double France became the first country to win both versions of the competition. The French men’s team won the 2001 FIFA U-17 World Championship in Trinidad and Tobago after defeating Nigeria 3-0 in the final. Eleven years later, France’s women’s team lifted the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Azerbaijan in 2012. They defeated North Korea 7-6 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the final to claim their maiden title. France therefore held the distinction of being the only country to have won both competitions until Nigeria’s latest achievement. Flamingos end Nigeria’s long wait Nigeria’s historic achievement was secured through a 2-1 victory over Japan in the 2026 final. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring in the 39th minute before Oluebube Umejiaku doubled Nigeria’s advantage two minutes into the second half. Japan reduced the deficit through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but the Flamingos held on to secure the trophy. The victory completed a remarkable campaign for the Nigerian side, which recovered from a 2-1 opening defeat to Poland to win its next six matches. The team also defeated Brazil 3-1 in the semi-finals to book its place in the final against Japan. The triumph was significant beyond Nigeria, as it marked the first time an African country had won the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. It also made the Flamingos the first Nigerian women’s national team to win a FIFA World Cup title. With the latest achievement, Nigeria joins France in the exclusive group of countries to have won both the men’s and women’s FIFA U-17 World Cups. nigeria.title: Presidency tackles Obi over alleged prevention from greeting Flamingos
nigeria.description: The Presidency has accused opposition politicians of attempting to politicise Nigeria’s national sports teams, following a claim by former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, that he was prevented from greeting members of the victorious Flamingos at an airport. The Special Assistant to the President on Social Media, Dada Olusegun, made the position known in a post on X on Monday, describing attempts to politicise national sports teams and institutions as distasteful. Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, had alleged that officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) stopped him from approaching the Under-17 women’s national team after their return from the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Reacting to the allegation, Olusegun said national athletes, including the Flamingos, represented the entire country rather than any political party or individual. He explained that protocols governing national teams were designed to protect young athletes from political exploitation, commercial distractions and unnecessary media attention while on official duties. “The constant attempt by the opposition to politicize our national sports teams and institutions is highly distasteful,” he wrote. “Our national athletes, including the Under-17 girls’ team, represent the entire Federal Republic of Nigeria, not any specific political party or individual ambition. Protocol guidelines around national teams are designed strictly to protect young athletes from political exploitation, commercial distractions, and unnecessary media circuses while on official duty.” Addressing Obi directly, the presidential aide urged him to reconsider what he described as his tendency to manipulate situations and rely on unverified accounts to create a narrative of victimisation. “Mr Peter Obi, I hope you will reflect on your manipulative way of life and stop weaponising unverified hearsay to build a victim narrative. Let our athletes focus on winning for Nigeria, free from political theatre,” he wrote. Obi had earlier said he arrived at the airport around 7am on Monday while preparing to travel to Enugu when he sighted the Flamingos, who had just returned from Morocco. He said he asked his protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether he could welcome the players but was informed that NFF officials had objected to his approach. According to Obi, the officials reportedly warned that they would lose their jobs if they allowed him to greet the team. The former governor also recalled an earlier incident on March 25, 2025, when he travelled to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, for a World Cup qualifying match and was allegedly prevented from greeting members of Nigeria’s national team after the game. Expressing concern over what he described as a growing culture of toxic politics, Obi said the country should prioritise unity and mutual respect regardless of political differences. Bakare clarified that his decision to stay outside the government should not be interpreted as opposition to the Tinubu administration, insisting that he had never belonged to the opposition. nigeria.title: UK lists categories of migrants who can secure permanent residence after 5 years
nigeria.description: The UK government has outlined categories of foreign nationals who will remain eligible to obtain permanent residence after five years, despite plans to extend the standard settlement period for most migrants to 10 years. Under its revised Earned Settlement policy, announced by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood on November 2, 2026, the government intends to replace the existing five-year standard route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) with a system that rewards migrants based on their earnings, professional contributions and immigration history. However, certain categories of migrants will retain access to the five-year settlement pathway. According to the Home Office, the exemptions are intended to recognise the contributions of higher-earning migrants, essential public service workers and people who have served the UK through specific immigration routes. Migrants who can qualify for permanent residence after five years The following groups have been identified under the revised settlement framework: 1. High-earning foreign workers Migrants earning more than £50,271 annually will be eligible to apply for permanent residence after five years, provided they meet the income requirement for at least three of the five years preceding their application. This category covers foreign professionals whose earnings meet the government’s specified threshold. 2. Doctors, nurses and teachers Foreign nationals working in qualifying healthcare and education occupations will retain the five-year settlement pathway. The government specifically identified doctors, nurses and teachers as examples of professionals whose contributions to essential public services justify a shorter route to permanent residence. 3. Eligible care workers Care workers who entered or switched into the social care route during the period between 2022 and 2025 will retain the opportunity to secure permanent residence after five years. However, they must have complied with their visa conditions and earned at least £25,000 annually while working in the social care sector. The government said the exemption recognises the contribution of care workers during the period when Britain’s social care sector faced significant staffing shortages following the COVID-19 pandemic. 4. Eligible family members of British citizens Certain partners, parents and children of British citizens will also retain access to the five-year settlement pathway. The exemption covers eligible family visa applicants, although the precise eligibility conditions will depend on the applicable immigration rules. 5. Refugees arriving through approved safe and legal routes Foreign nationals granted refugee status after arriving in the UK through government-approved safe and legal routes will be eligible to apply for permanent residence after five years. nigeria.description: … add two new charges By Demola Akinyemi Ilorin In a dramatic twist, the Kwara State Government has filed an amendment to its initial 20-count charge against its two former governors, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki and Alhaji Abdulfatai Ahmed, over the 2018 Offa bank robbery case by dropping 18 of the original charges while retaining only two and adding two new charges. In the amended charge sheet with Charge Number KWS/114C/2026 signed by the State Attorney General, Senior Ibrahim Sulyman (SAN), sighted by journalists in Ilorin, the government by implication has now reduced the total number of charges to four. In the new charge sheet, Counts 1 and 2 accused Saraki, Ahmed, Yusuf Abdulwahab and Alabi Olalekan of “conspiring to belong to a gang of thieves” and “belonging to a gang of thieves”. Also, counts 3 and 4, accused the quartet of concealment and disappearance of a “vehicle used for illegal purpose”. A motion on notice for the amended charges dated November 6th, 2026, has been filed by the prosecution and supported by a 6-paragraph affidavit deposed to by Sulyman Mohammed-Jamiu, a litigation clerk in the office of the Kwara State AG. It will be recalled that at the last sitting of the State High Court on the case on November 5th, 2026, the judge, Justice Osuolale Ajayi, reserved his ruling on the issue of whether he could continue with the arraignment while the defendant has a pending application for a stay of proceedings on the matter at the Court of Appeal. The Court of Appeal on November 3rd, 2026, advised the lawyer, Abdulfatah Ahmed, J. A. Mumini, SAN, to formally make his application for the court to issue an order that the parties at the trial court should maintain status quo ante bellum instead of the oral submission that he made to the court. The appellate court then adjourned the case to November 12, 2026. The case at the trial court which commenced in April 2026 has not proceeded to trial as the court is still mired in several preliminary issues which have been taken to the appellate court. Contacted, a member of Saraki and Ahmed’s legal team described the struggle by the prosecution to press charges against the two former governors as “a mockery of the judicial process and an exercise in futility”. Vanguard reliably gathered that failure to make any headway by the Kwara state government may not be unconnected to the two pieces of legal advice issued in 2018 by the Office of the Federal Director of Public Prosecutions in the Office of the Attorney General of the Federation, who, after reviewing the police investigation file on the Offa robbery case in 2018, concluded that there is no evidence remotely or directly linking Saraki or Ahmed to the Offa robbery incident. nigeria.title: UK issues guide for Nigerians, other nationals on accessing eVisa
nigeria.description: The United Kingdom has released guidelines explaining how visa holders, including Nigerians, can access their electronic immigration status. UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) published the instructions in an infographic shared on its official X account on Monday, outlining the process of setting up an account, confirming one’s identity and connecting it to an eVisa. An eVisa is an online record containing a person’s identity and immigration status. It shows the category of permission granted to an individual, including whether they have indefinite leave to remain in the UK, as well as the conditions attached to their immigration status. The UK government said electronic visas have replaced physical immigration documents, adding that individuals granted a UK visa or other permission to remain in the country would be issued an eVisa. How to apply for and access a UK eVisa 1. Submit a visa application Applicants must first complete the UK visa application process through the government’s official website, GOV.UK . Depending on the category of application, they may also need to provide biometric details and verify their identity at a designated Visa Application Centre. 2. Receive an application decision After submitting their applications, applicants will be notified by email once UK Visas and Immigration reaches a decision. The agency advises applicants to monitor their spam and junk folders to ensure they do not miss important notifications. 3. Set up a UKVI account Those whose applications are approved should proceed to create an account through the official eVisa portal at gov.uk/evisa. Applicants are required to follow the online instructions until the system confirms that their accounts have been successfully created. 4. Confirm identity and connect the eVisa After creating an account, users must log in and verify their identities using the UK Immigration: ID Check application. They are also required to link their UKVI accounts to their electronic immigration records to make the eVisas accessible online. 5. Access the electronic visa Once the eVisa is available, users will receive an email notification directing them to view their immigration status online. UKVI advises holders to review their digital records and ensure that all personal and immigration details are accurate before travelling. The UK government says creating a UKVI account and viewing an eVisa are free of charge. The post UK issues guide for Nigerians, other nationals on accessing eVisa appeared first on Vanguard News .

He cautioned journalists against spreading misinformation, unverified results, manipulated videos and inflammatory political narratives capable of undermining public confidence and triggering violence. nigeria.title: CHOGM 2026: Bianca seeks stronger commonwealth cooperation
nigeria.description: Nigeria has called for stronger cooperation among Commonwealth member states to address security challenges, expand trade, strengthen democratic institutions and promote climate resilience. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, disclosed this on Monday in a post on her X account, detailing Nigeria’s expectations from the Commonwealth following her interventions at the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua. She said Nigeria emphasised the need for collective action on peace and security, trade, climate resilience and youth empowerment, particularly in combating terrorism and expanding access to development finance. Odumegwu-Ojukwu also drew attention to Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 general elections, stressing the importance of supporting free, fair and credible electoral processes through election monitoring groups and stronger democratic institutions across member states. According to her, Nigeria, under President Bola Tinubu’s leadership, remains committed to promoting democracy, consensus, civil, political and social rights, while upholding the rule of law and judicial independence. She described the creation of the Commonwealth Trade Portal as a welcome development, noting that trade facilitation initiatives would promote economic growth, strengthen trade links among member states and help developing economies integrate into the global financial market. The minister further urged the Commonwealth to give greater attention to women and girls affected by conflicts, displacement and climate change. She said their access to essential services, livelihood opportunities and justice should remain central to collective responses, adding that their voices must shape solutions to the challenges they face. On reparatory justice, Odumegwu-Ojukwu identified the agenda as a major highlight of the ministerial meeting, particularly the agreement by the United Kingdom government to engage in structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected countries over the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical consequences. She said Nigeria hoped that the commitments adopted at CHOGM 2026 would translate into practical actions capable of creating jobs, strengthening security and improving the lives of citizens across Commonwealth member states. nigeria.title: Musiala’s condition cannot be cured, may never return to best — Bayern president
nigeria.description: Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness has raised concerns over Jamal Musiala’s long-term future, saying the Germany international is suffering from a condition that cannot be permanently cured and may never regain his previous level of performance. According to BBC Sport, Hoeness said the 23-year-old forward’s condition could only be managed to some extent with medication, leaving the club uncertain about whether he would return to his best. “We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,” Hoeness told Bavarian broadcaster BR24. He also questioned whether Musiala would ever recover the level he displayed before his health problems, while acknowledging that Bayern would continue to support the player, who is under contract until 2030. “But the question remains: will he one day be able to regain the level he used to show?” Hoeness said. Hoeness further suggested that the situation had created a contractual dilemma for the German champions, claiming Musiala’s condition was not covered by the insurance attached to his deal. “Imagine if Bayern Munich now decided to question his contract, and told him: what you are able to offer currently no longer matches the level stipulated in the contract,” he said. Musiala’s health concerns emerged during pre-season after he collapsed twice within four days. He was subsequently reported to have a treatable neurological dysfunction. The forward has also been sidelined by a hamstring injury sustained in September and has yet to feature for Bayern since then, although he has recently returned to training. He has scored twice in four appearances for the German champions in all competitions this season. Former Bayern and Germany captain Lothar Matthaus, however, interpreted Hoeness’ comments as an attempt to challenge and motivate the youngster rather than write him off. “He’s needling him a little. It’s not just about wrapping him in cotton wool. He also has to battle against adversity sometimes,” Matthaus told Sky90. Matthaus added that Hoeness wanted Musiala to respond to the remarks by proving he could return to his previous level. “Uli was looking to create that adversity with this statement. “It’s fine for him to say something like that, because we can’t just put a positive spin on things and somehow wait for him to come back. “If I were in Jamal Musiala’s position, that would be motivation enough to show Uli I’m back.” Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea’s academy and has since scored 71 goals and provided 38 assists in 235 appearances for the club. He has earned 46 caps for Germany and shared the Golden Boot as joint-top scorer at Euro 2024. business.title: U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have formally withdrawn a 2020 proposal that would have cut the Bank Secrecy Act threshold for cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250 and spelled out that the rules cover crypto, leaving the existing $3,000 line in place. The notice, published Monday in the Federal Register, says the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Fed’s Board of Governors “will not take further action” on a proposal they first issued on Oct. 27, 2020. That plan would have lowered the recordkeeping and Travel Rule thresholds to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. Those rules require banks and nonbank financial institutions to collect, retain and pass along customer information on transfers of $3,000 or more. It also would have clarified the meaning of “money” in both rules so they apply to transactions involving convertible virtual currency, along with digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. Why the agencies backed off Per the notcie, FinCEN and the Fed received nearly 3,000 comments on the proposal, most of them substantially similar form letters. Commenters generally opposed the lower threshold, arguing that it would burden smaller institutions and could push consumers sending remittances toward less regulated channels. Many also noted that potentially illicit transfers below $3,000 were already being flagged to FinCEN through suspicious activity reports. Several said the threshold should rise instead, citing inflation since 1995. Sentiment on the crypto language was mixed. Companies that provide crypto services and their trade groups opposed it, citing technical limits and the lack of an international messaging standard for crypto transfers, while some banks and money services businesses supported it. The agencies gave two reasons for pulling the proposal. More than five years have passed, and they said more public feedback would help before adopting anything similar. The withdrawal, they wrote, gives the public “certainty” that no final rule will be issued without another chance to comment. The second reason is the crypto industry itself. The notice says crypto markets “have continued to mature” and new legal frameworks are emerging, citing the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted on July 18, 2025. Any future change tied to crypto, the agencies said, should be considered in light of those developments so it is “fit for purpose.” What the withdrawal does and does not do The notice does not repeal or amend any rule. The $3,000 threshold that has applied for decades stays where it is, and so does the existing Travel Rule. What disappears is the specific path to $250 and the proposed wording that would have written crypto into the definition of money. The agencies did not say whether they plan a new proposal or offer a timeline. The withdrawal is the latest in a run of reversals from Treasury. On Oct.

business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Wins Full Federal Trust Charter From OCC Coinbase has won a full national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, upgrading the conditional approval it received in April and putting its institutional custody business under direct federal supervision, the exchange said Monday. The OCC approved the application for Coinbase National Trust Company last Friday, the company said in a blog post. OCC licensing records, as reported, show the chartering process was completed Nov. 6. Coinbase applied in October 2025 and received preliminary approval on April 2. In the intervening months it had to finish its organizational and operational preparations before the OCC would let the trust bank open. “This charter allows us to bring clear and consistent federal uniformity to our industry-leading custody capabilities,” Coinbase wrote, adding that it strengthens the regulatory framework under which it serves customers. The company said it has served as a custodian for more than 14 years. What the charter allows A national trust bank can hold assets for clients as a fiduciary, and Coinbase’s focus is custody for institutional customers. It is not a commercial bank. It cannot take ordinary retail deposits or make loans, and the charter does not authorize it to issue stablecoins. Staking, prime trading and financing will keep running through Coinbase affiliates, not the trust itself. Under the OCC’s April decision, the trust bank acts as an intermediary for those services and does not perform them directly. The decision also sets conditions. The trust bank must hold at least $60 million in Tier 1 capital and enough liquid assets to cover 180 days of operating expenses during its first three years. The license does not automatically connect Coinbase to Federal Reserve payment systems either. That requires a separate application under the Fed’s account access guidelines. Coinbase already runs custody through Coinbase Custody Trust Company, a limited-purpose trust regulated by the New York State Department of Financial Services. The company plans to move that business to the national entity over three years. A crowded charter queue Coinbase is the latest crypto firm to complete a federal trust charter. Ripple received final approval on Oct. 26, and Circle won final OCC approval in July, a decision that put USDC reserves on a path toward federal supervision. The OCC has been courting the sector. In August, Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould said “America and the OCC are once again open for business,” as the regulator touted its charter push. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Two people can earn the same salary and end up in completely different places ten years later, simply because one converted part of that income into assets and the other converted all of it into lifestyle. entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. Redditch United player Dan Sweeney said he was targeted by a Kettering supporter during Saturday's Southern League Premier Division Central tie at the Poppies' Latimer Park stadium, which the hosts won 2-1. The incident comes after a match official reported alleged racial abuse at a Kettering fixture last season , and a previous instance of alleged racist abuse against a Redditch player at Latimer Park in 2017 . In a statement, Kettering director of football Fabian Forde said the "poison" of racism went beyond matchdays. He also spoke out against the presence of what he called "festering" racism on the club's fans forums. Writing on the club's website , Forde said: "Let's be completely honest with ourselves: this is not the first time. We can no longer hide behind the comforting lie that 'it's just a small minority' or 'they don't reflect the majority of our fans'. "Every single time we dismiss hate by calling it a minority issue, we minimise the damage. The truth is, if the majority stays silent, that small minority becomes our identity. "They tarnish our reputation in the eyes of opposition players, fans, and officials. They make our club look like a haven for bigotry. Is that really who we want to be?" Forde added that the club could not "keep sending out generic statements that mean nothing" and urged fans to support "real cultural change" by taking responsibility for calling out the perpetrators of racist abuse. He said: "To the majority of our fans, the good, decent people who love this club for the right reasons, we are pleading with you. "We need you to stand up. We need you to confront this minority head-on. If you see someone typing hate online, call them out. If you hear someone shouting abuse next to you on a Saturday afternoon, don't look away. sports.title: Today in Motorsport History, November 9: Rosberg Won the 2014 Brazilian Grand Prix as Hamilton’s Spin Kept the Title Fight Alive
sports.description: Nico Rosberg in the Mercedes F1 W05 Hybrid at Suzuka during the 2014 Japanese Grand Prix. Illustrative image, not from the Brazilian Grand Prix. Photo: Takayuki Suzuki / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0) Nico Rosberg won the 2014 Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos on November 9, 2014, beating Mercedes teammate Lewis Hamilton by 1.457 seconds. Hamilton’s spin on lap 28 decided the race, and the result trimmed his championship lead to 17 points with one round left, a finale that was going to pay double points. What happened at the 2014 Brazilian Grand Prix Rosberg took pole position with a 1:10.023 and led the early laps of the 71-lap race. He pitted from the lead on lap 7 and Hamilton followed a lap later, which let Nico Hülkenberg, on a different strategy, lead for a handful of laps. Rosberg passed Hülkenberg for the lead on lap 14, and Hamilton did the same a lap after that, setting up a two-car Mercedes fight. The swing came after the second round of stops. Rosberg pitted on lap 26 and handed Hamilton the lead, but Hamilton’s tyres were finished. On lap 28 he locked his rear tyres under braking, spun onto the run-off area, and rejoined 7.4 seconds behind Rosberg. Rosberg made his last stop around lap 50, stayed in front, and held off Hamilton over the final laps. Hamilton set the fastest lap, a 1:13.555 on lap 62, and still finished 1.457 seconds adrift. Formula 1’s own race analysis described it as a dominant Rosberg performance that set up the title decider. Lewis Hamilton in the Mercedes F1 W05 Hybrid at Suzuka during the 2014 Japanese Grand Prix. Illustrative image, not from the Brazilian Grand Prix. Photo: Takayuki Suzuki / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0) Felipe Massa completed the podium for Williams, 41.031 seconds back, even after a five-second penalty for speeding in the pit lane. Jenson Button was fourth, Sebastian Vettel fifth and Fernando Alonso sixth. The one-two was Mercedes’ 11th of the season, a Formula 1 record at the time. The competitive context: a title fight with a strange rulebook Hamilton arrived in São Paulo 24 points clear of Rosberg, 316 to 292. Brazil could not settle anything, because the Abu Dhabi finale was set to award double points. Even if Hamilton had won and Rosberg had scored nothing, Rosberg would still have been 49 points back and mathematically alive. Rosberg’s win, worth 25 points to Hamilton’s 18, moved the totals to 334 and 317. That left Rosberg needing to win the finale and have Hamilton finish third or lower. Anything else, and the champion was Hamilton. The same Interlagos circuit had produced a one-point title swing before; we covered it in our look at Hamilton’s last-corner pass on Glock in 2008 and in Räikkönen’s one-point title in 2007 . sports.description: El Paso boxer Nayeli Rodriguez earned arguably her best professional win via split decision against unbeaten Nat Dove in a super flyweight matchup. sports.title: Open Championship returning to Carnoustie in 2029 for first time in 11 years
sports.description: The Open Championship is returning to Carnoustie in 2029. The R&A announced Monday that the 157th edition of the oldest major championship in the world would return to Carnoustie for the ninth time. The last Open held at the venue was 2018, when Francesco Molinari held off Tiger Woods and others for his lone major title. Other winners at Carnoustie include Tommy Armour, Sir Henry Cotton, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Tom Watson, Paul Lawrie and Padraig Harrington. “Carnoustie is a world-class championship venue where some of golf’s greatest players have lifted the Claret Jug and the return of The Open to these famous links after more than a decade will give fans the opportunity to be part of another memorable chapter in the Championship’s history," R&A executive chief Mark Darbon said. “We want to continue to deliver an outstanding experience for players, fans and our partners at one of the world’s great sporting events and so have worked closely in collaboration with Carnoustie to help ensure their plans to enhance the venue also support successful stagings of The Open in the years ahead. “We are grateful to Carnoustie’s ownership and management, the Scottish Government and local authorities for their support in bringing The Open back to Angus and look forward to another memorable Championship in 2029.” The 157th Open Championship is set for July 19-22, 2029. The Open will head to St. Andrews in 2027 before going to Royal Lytham and St. Annes in August 2028, moving back a month to accommodate the Olympic Games in Los Angeles. Ryan Fox won the 2026 Open at Royal Birkdale. Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. sports.title: Ajsa Sivka drawing Elena Delle Donne comparisons is a terrifying warning to the SEC
sports.description: Kentucky women’s basketball head coach Kenny Brooks already called Ajsa Sivka his best passer, but after Sunday’s shootout against No. 25 NC State, the first-year wing from Slovenia proved she might just be the best overall player on the Kentucky roster. Sivka completely took over the game against the Wolfpack. She exploded for 32 points and tied a program record with eight 3-pointers. She got to the rim at will, threaded brilliant passes through the defense, and officially broke onto the national scene, with television announcers comparing her to college basketball legend Elena Delle Donne. For fans who follow international basketball, this breakout performance was not a surprise. The 6-foot-4 guard was selected 10th overall by the Chicago Sky in the 2025 WNBA Draft, but she opted to remain in Europe to represent Slovenia in the FIBA Women’s European Basketball Championship. During that tournament run, she shot 50 percent from the floor, highlighted by a flawless 4-of-4 performance from deep against Italy. That elite efficiency earned her MVP honors at the 2023 FIBA U18 European Championship. But the comparison is what excites me. For those unfamiliar with the women’s game, Delle Donne is an absolute legend. During her historic career at Delaware, Delle Donne was the ultimate mismatch. She was a towering perimeter player who could handle the ball, shoot from anywhere, and score at will. She led the entire nation in scoring as a junior with 28.1 points per game and once dropped 54 points in a single contest. Delle Donne was a dominant force who carried her team deep into the NCAA Tournament, combining elite frontcourt size with traditional guard skills and scoring over half of Delaware’s points, finishing with 33 in a loss to No. 2 seed Kentucky, 69-62, in 2013. Overall, Sivka was 11-for-17 from the floor and 8-for-12 from deep. sports.title: Rangers Daily: Korpisalo ‘going to get better;’ Devils Hellebuyck decision
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Joonas Koripsalo is a pretty low-key guy. So, it wasn’t a big surprise that the veteran goalie was pretty matter of fact when discussing his first start and win for the New York Rangers on Saturday night in Seattle. “I felt OK, there’s still some stuff to clean up, and it’s obviously going to get better as we go along,” Korpisalo said postgame , after the Rangers skated to a 4-3 victory over the Kraken . He’s right, of course. There’s stuff to clean up and it should get better moving forward — for him and the team. The Rangers led 4-0 before surrendering three third-period goals to sweat out, what turned out to be, their third consecutive victory. Korpisalo made 25 saves in his Rangers debut — one that was delayed by more than a month after a foot infection sidelined him after he backed up Igor Shesterkin on opening night against his former team, the Boston Bruins. You know the rest of the story. Shesterkin sustained a season-ending knee injury, rookie Dylan Garand — fresh off clearing waivers — played 12 games in a row (10 starts, two in relief), and Rangers nation eagerly awaited Korpisalo’s return. The irony there is rich, of course, considering most fans didn’t want the 32-year-old goalie in the first place, when the Rangers traded for him this past summer. Garand was the chosen one to be No. 2 behind Shesterkin on Broadway. But now, everyone realized Garand needs a proven NHL partner to share the goaltending load with Shesterkin done for the season. “You know what it takes, right? So, all that time I was working out, making sure I’m as ready as possible to go when it’s my time to play,” Korpisalo said about knowing how to prepare himself as a veteran when he was sidelined. This isn’t the return of Shesterkin, perhaps the best goalie in the sport. But Korpisalo’s return is important to the Rangers because it brings balance to the goaltending position, gives the team two viable options to play each night, and should bring out the best in a more rested Garand. technology.title: Who Gives A Crap? Hackers, apparently, after toilet paper maker's customer data exposed
technology.description: Toilet paper purveyor Who Gives A Crap has found itself in a bit of a mess after an intruder accessed customer information through a third-party software provider, leaving the company scrambling to clean up a breach affecting shoppers in the UK, US, and Australia. In an email sent to affected customers over the weekend, seen by The Register , the loo roll seller warns that personal information was accessed without authorization after a security incident at an unnamed US-based marketing software provider. The email explains that the intruder gained access to the supplier's systems on October 30. The provider spotted the intrusion the following day and says it secured its systems by November 1, although Who Gives A Crap wasn't told until November 6. It's unclear why the supplier sat on the bad news for another five days before passing it on. The exposed information includes customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, mailing addresses, and total spending with the company. In other words, someone may now know not only where you live, but just how much of your hard-earned cash you've flushed down the crapper. Payment information, order details, and passwords were not involved, and customers' accounts were not directly accessed. That's something of a relief, although whether the intruder actually made off with the data remains a pressing question. "We don't yet know whether the information was copied or downloaded," the company told customers, adding that it had found no evidence of misuse. In a separate public statement , Who Gives A Crap co-founder and CEO Simon Griffiths confirmed that the incident affected customers across the company's Australian, UK, and US stores. Canadian customers, meanwhile, appear to have escaped this particular toilet emergency, with the supplier reporting that no personal information belonging to shoppers in the country was accessed. Who Gives A Crap says it has since disconnected the provider from its systems, changed access credentials, and begun warning affected customers to watch out for suspicious emails, texts, calls, and other unsolicited communications. "The main concern is scam or phishing messages that use your real details to look convincing," the company warned in its customer email. While Who Gives A Crap has been busy cleaning up, the supplier at the center of this particular stink remains a mystery. The company hasn't identified the software provider or disclosed how many customers were affected, including those in the UK, and didn’t respond to our questions. Griffiths said the company is "engaging with the relevant regulatory authorities, as required." In the UK, the ICO told The Register : "We can confirm Who Gives A Crap Limited has reported an incident and we are assessing the information provided." Who Gives A Crap has plenty of toilet paper to hand, although cleaning up this particular situation might require more than a few rolls. ®

technology.title: The AI bubble can wait, but your exit plan can't
technology.description: The AI bubble isn't about to burst, Forrester reckons, although businesses should prepare for a correction that could upend their suppliers, contracts, and prices. Spending on infrastructure has raced ahead of measurable returns, the analyst says, yet the financial strength of the companies funding the build-out is what keep Forrester from predicting an imminent crash. "Fears that an AI bubble is about to burst are premature," said Forrester emerging technology veep Brian Hopkins. "About nine-tenths of the money building today's AI computing infrastructure comes from large, healthy technology companies paying out of their own cash flow. The risk is concentrated in a few places: a small number of builders under real financial strain, and circular financing deals with the AI labs." Conveniently, Forrester has developed an AI Bubble Model to help technology leaders monitor the risks and prepare. Its latest report, " An AI Bubble Burst Is Not Imminent ," notes what many in the IT industry, including The Register , have been saying for a while: that the hyperscale operators are committing a record share of revenue into capital expenditure to bring online more infrastructure to support AI development and use. At the same time, the boost in productivity doesn't justify this supplier capacity build-out. Forrester calculates that the infrastructure investments break even only if AI raises US GDP by 5 percent by 2035. Published estimates suggest productivity improvements could provide about two percentage points of that uplift, leaving roughly $1.3 trillion to come from other sources of value. A recent report from management consultants Bain & Company came to similar conclusions, estimating the AI industry needs to generate $6 trillion in annual revenue by 2031 to keep funding all the infrastructure it needs, and this will require new uses beyond simply enhancing employee productivity. Forrester also claims that the forces making AI abundant also make parts of the market unstable, and says that enterprise users should take heed of how prices collapsed as major providers like Anthropic slashed token costs in response to competition from open source models. If demand disappoints as new capacity comes online, suppliers could cut investment, merge, change prices, or discontinue products. Customers could find themselves rebuilding AI plans around suppliers and services that no longer exist. Forrester advises businesses to track whether their AI projects deliver measurable value and limit their exposure to vulnerable suppliers – with its help, of course. Companies can judge how things are going by looking at the gap between suppliers' contracted business and revenue actually recognized, along with how they fund their build-outs. If a vendor leans more on outside investment and customer prepayments, as Oracle and CoreWeave have, this is a red flag to cut back dependencies on them, Forrester says.
